analysis_notes.torah_summary: Torah #264 is a very short teaching (3 sentences). Its central argument: pgam habrit = diverting shefa from holiness; tzedakah = restoring shefa to holiness; therefore tzedakah rectifies the bris. The bechina language appears once: the verse about the Mishkan donation (men coming to women) is called the 'bechina of zivug accomplished through tzedakah'. The Torah then notes that giving to an unworthy pauper compounds the pgam because it again misdirects shefa — establishing an implicit bechina between the two acts of misdirected flow (sexual pgam and tzedakah-to-wrong-recipient). The good/evil mirror: proper shefa to kedusah vs. misdirected shefa to impurity. A minimal bechina package could be built around these concepts if edges were added.
